title: ADDCOLUMNS(SUMMARIZE()) — use SUMMARIZECOLUMNS instead
description: ADDCOLUMNS wrapping SUMMARIZE creates an intermediate table then adds columns. SUMMARIZECOLUMNS is a single optimized operation that handles both grouping and aggregation.

title: FILTER(ALL(Table)) — iterates the whole expanded table
description: FILTER(ALL(Table), …) iterates every row of the expanded table (AP-11: a measure predicate here materializes the whole table in the Formula Engine). When the predicate reads only columns of that table (the canon's running-total form, rule 14) the finding is info - FILTER(ALL(Table[Col]), …) is the lighter form. The column form FILTER(ALL(Table[Col]), …) is exactly what a CALCULATE boolean filter expands to and is not flagged.
fix_suggestion: Filter only the columns you need: FILTER(ALL(Table[Col]), …) or a CALCULATE boolean filter.

title: FILTER(ALLSELECTED(Table)) — iterates the whole expanded table
description: FILTER(ALLSELECTED(Table), …) iterates every row of the expanded table. The column form FILTER(ALLSELECTED(Table[Col]), …) is not flagged.
fix_suggestion: Filter only the columns you need: FILTER(ALLSELECTED(Table[Col]), …).

title: Deeply nested CALCULATE (>2 levels)
description: More than 2 levels of nested CALCULATE creates complex filter context transitions that are hard to optimize and reason about. Each level adds context-transition overhead.
fix_suggestion: Flatten nested CALCULATE by combining filter conditions or extracting into VARs

title: COUNTROWS(VALUES(col)) — consider DISTINCTCOUNT
description: COUNTROWS(VALUES(column)) counts the distinct values of one column and can be written as DISTINCTCOUNT(column). Not flagged when the argument is a table (DISTINCTCOUNT(table) is invalid) or the result is compared to a constant (COUNTROWS(VALUES(col)) = 1 is the HASONEVALUE idiom). DISTINCTCOUNT is SE-bound (DCOUNT does not scale across cores): MS DAX011 says to benchmark it against SUMX(DISTINCT(col), 1).
fix_suggestion: Benchmark DISTINCTCOUNT(column) against COUNTROWS(VALUES(column)) / SUMX(DISTINCT(column), 1) in a trace before changing it.

title: RELATED inside iterator
description: RELATED inside an iterator is normally resolved by the storage engine as a join and is the idiomatic way to multiply by a dimension attribute. Informational: only worth revisiting on very large tables or limited (cross-source / many-to-many) relationships.
fix_suggestion: Consider CALCULATE with RELATEDTABLE or denormalize the column into the fact table

title: LOOKUPVALUE — prefer RELATED with physical relationship
description: LOOKUPVALUE performs a linear scan. If a relationship exists between the tables, RELATED uses the indexed relationship path and is significantly faster.
fix_suggestion: Create a relationship between the tables and use RELATED(column) instead

title: EARLIER/EARLIEST is discouraged — use VAR
description: EARLIER and EARLIEST navigate row contexts by ordinal position (discouraged, not removed; still needed in calculated columns on old models). VAR to capture the current row value is clearer and not position-dependent.
fix_suggestion: Capture the value with VAR _currentValue = [Column] before the inner iterator, then reference _currentValue

title: IF(ISBLANK(x), <constant>, …) converts BLANK to a value
description: IF(ISBLANK([x]), 0, [x]) turns BLANK into a value, so every row/cell of the grain becomes non-empty (dense) — more work and more memory. The sparsity-preserving form IF(ISBLANK([x]), BLANK(), …) is not flagged.
fix_suggestion: Allow BLANK propagation where possible, or use COALESCE([x], 0) only when truly needed

title: COUNTROWS(DISTINCT()) — use DISTINCTCOUNT instead
description: COUNTROWS(DISTINCT(column)) counts the distinct values of one column and can be written as DISTINCTCOUNT(column); benchmark first (MS DAX011). Not flagged for a table argument or a comparison with a constant.

title: VALUES in scalar context — prefer SELECTEDVALUE
description: When VALUES is used to get a single value (e.g., in IF or variable assignment), SELECTEDVALUE is more explicit and handles multi-value gracefully with an alternate result.
fix_suggestion: Use SELECTEDVALUE(column, alternateResult) for clearer intent

title: CALCULATETABLE(FILTER()) — redundant wrapping
description: CALCULATETABLE(FILTER(<table>, <column predicate>), …) is redundant: CALCULATETABLE takes the Boolean predicate directly. Not flagged when the predicate reads a measure, another table or a column-set first argument (FILTER(ALL(col), [M] > x) cannot be a Boolean filter).
fix_suggestion: Replace with CALCULATETABLE(Table, filter_condition) without FILTER wrapper

title: NATURALLEFTOUTERJOIN forces FE evaluation
description: NATURALLEFTOUTERJOIN is fully evaluated in the Formula Engine and cannot be pushed to the Storage Engine. NATURALINNERJOIN over precomputed key sets is the Microsoft-preferred shape (MS DAX021) and is not flagged. Consider SUMMARIZECOLUMNS or model relationships.
fix_suggestion: Use model relationships with SUMMARIZECOLUMNS or CALCULATE where possible

title: GENERATE forces nested iteration in FE
description: GENERATE evaluates the second table expression for every row of the first, entirely in the Formula Engine. For large tables, this is extremely slow.
fix_suggestion: Use SUMMARIZECOLUMNS or model relationships to achieve the same result with SE optimization
